items.title: Police organize 2-day conference to fight theft in Mississauga
items.summary: Peel Regional Police are taking the fight against retail theft to the boardroom — at least for two days. The local police force, tasked to battle crime in Mississauga and Brampton, is hosting a province-wide Retail Organized Crime Conference Tuesday and Wednesday at the Hyatt Place Toronto in Mississauga. “The two-day conference brings together law enforcement agencies, retail industry leaders and public safety partners from across Ontario to discuss emerging trends, investigative best practices and partnership-driven solutions to disrupt organized retail crime networks,” Peel police said in a news release Monday. The conference gets underway Tuesday morning. Peel Regional Police Chief Nishan Duraiappah and Peel police Deputy Chief Marc Andrews along with Peel Police Service Board vice-chair Omar Khan will welcome conference guests that include Ontario Solicitor Genera Michael Kerzner and the Retail Council of Canada’s Rui Rodrigues. When not talking about ways to reduce retail theft, police in Peel say they’ve been delivering blows to those who commit such crimes in Mississauga and Brampton. Peel Regional Police formed a specialized unit of officers in September 2025 to tackle crime that includes break-ins and the taking from retail businesses of large amounts of goods such as jewelry, clothes and other items. Speaking at a press conference in July at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga’s downtown core, Andrews said the force’s increased focus on a crime that’s “become endemic in our community” has paid off so far.

items.title: Milev's Clear Air wins thrilling J/24 North American Championship at Port Credit Yacht Club
items.summary: Rossi Milev of Canada and his team aboard Clear Air won the 2026 J/24 North American Championship, hosted by Port Credit Yacht Club in Mississauga, Ontario, Canada from September 30-October 4. In a tightly contested regatta featuring 24 boats from the United States and Canada, including 18 Corinthian teams, Milev relied on consistency to secure the victory without winning a race in the eight-race series. The Championship came down to the final day, with just three points separating the top five teams heading into Sunday's racing. After an unsettled morning brought an onshore postponement, the fleet launched at noon as the breeze settled into the southwest and built to 15 knots, with gusts to 20. The waves grew to their largest of the regatta, providing a challenging finale for the fleet. Race Committee completed two races before the time limit for the dramatic conclusion. Milev's Clear Air faced a challenging position heading into the final day's racing, having sat as low as ninth at one point before climbing back to fifth. With a scoreline of 3-2-2-10-4-2-2-4 and discarding the 10th-place finish, Milev finished with 19 net points and the continental title. Canada's Evan Petley-Jones' Lifted finished second overall with 21 points, just two behind the champion. Petley-Jones topped the Corinthian division, followed by Jay Miles' Blister and Mike Stasko's Redine. Kurt Dammeier's Amuse Bouche completed the overall podium in third with 22 points, just one point behind Lifted. Paul Abdullah's Tremendous Slouch placed fourth with 26 points, while Michael Goldfarb's WarCanoe rounded out the top five with 37 points. The Championship highlighted the resurgence of the Canadian J/24 Class, with strong participation from both sides of the border and a deep field of experienced sailors.

items.title: Latest polls show tight race for mayor in Mississauga
items.summary: Given results from the latest polls, it appears the hotly contested mayoral race in Mississauga is up for grabs with three weeks remaining until election night. Two of three polls to release results the past couple of days have former mayor Bonnie Crombie with narrow leads over Mayor Carolyn Parrish while a third shows the incumbent with a nine-point advantage over her predecessor. Liaison Strategies said Monday morning its latest Mississauga Tracker survey finds Crombie at 30 per cent, Parrish at 29 per cent, Ward 2 Coun. Alvin Tedjo at 26 per cent and Ward 7 Coun. items.title: Jetliner Road Shut Down After Driver Strikes Pedestrian Near Pearson Airport Monday Morning
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel police say a pedestrian was taken to hospital Monday morning after being struck by a vehicle at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga. Police did not release details about the pedestrian beyond confirming the injuries were minor. Investigators also did not disclose what kind of vehicle was involved in the collision. Police closed westbound Jetliner Road at Airport Road following the crash and asked drivers to find alternate routes. Officers did not say how long the closure would last. Insauga notes Monday's crash was the second time in less than a week that a pedestrian has been struck by a vehicle on a busy Mississauga road.

items.title: Tedjo Doubles His Support Since August as Liaison Poll Shows Mississauga Mayoral Race Tightening to Three Ways
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a new Liaison Strategies poll conducted after last Thursday's debate found Mississauga's mayoral race tightening into a genuine three-way contest. Among decided and leaning voters, Bonnie Crombie came in at 30 per cent, Mayor Carolyn Parrish at 29 per cent and councillor Alvin Tedjo at 26 per cent, with Dipika Damerla at 11 per cent. David Valentin, principal at Liaison Strategies, told the Star the numbers show what is beginning to look like a three-way race. Valentin said Tedjo's climb may reflect undecided voters responding to the campaigns' bigger moves, pointing to Crombie's push for a subway extension and Tedjo's endorsement from the Peel Police union. He added that Tedjo's affordability-focused platform, including a proposed property tax freeze and a new deferral program for seniors, appears to be resonating given that affordability remains voters' top concern. The Star notes Tedjo sat at just 9 per cent in a similar Liaison poll taken in mid-August, when Crombie and Parrish were tied at 35 per cent among decided and leaning voters.

items.title: A Pandemic-Era Walk to a Mississauga Marsh Turned Into a Yearslong Conservation Mission for One Family
items.summary: According to The Pointer, Iyah, now a Mississauga tween, first noticed Osprey Marsh in the Lisgar neighbourhood back in fall 2020, when she was four years old and her family had just moved into the area during the pandemic. Iyah told the outlet the park's giant animal mural was impossible to miss from the car, and that it became one of the few places still open to her family while schools and activities shut down around them. She says she asked her mother, Jenna Evans, to take her to see it, and Evans agreed after weeks spent unpacking their new home. The Pointer reports the marsh sits a 10-minute walk from their house, near Ninth Line and Britannia Road West. Up close, mother and daughter found the animals painted on the mural were species that actually live in the marsh itself. That first visit marked the start of what has grown into Iyah's ongoing effort, years later, to protect the green space she found during one of the pandemic's quietest stretches.
